name: Dentin Dysplasia

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiographic Diagnostic Criteria for Dentin Dysplasia

criteria.description: Presence of short, malformed, or absent roots on dental radiographs
Clinically normal enamel with abnormal dentin structure
Radiographic evidence of pulp chamber obliteration or pulp stones
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic radiographic root abnormalities and pulpal calcifications with clinically normal enamel
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily radiographic supported by clinical findings and family history

imaging: Radiographs showing short, malformed, or absent roots
Pulp chamber obliteration or pulp stones on dental X-rays
genetic: Mutations in the DSPP gene associated with autosomal dominant inheritance
other: Normal enamel clinically despite dentin abnormalities

distinguishingFeatures: More generalized enamel and dentin involvement
Different genetic mutations (DSPP but distinct phenotype)
Ghost-like appearance of teeth on radiographs
Involvement of enamel and dentin with hypoplasia

redFlags: Premature tooth loss in absence of trauma or caries
Recurrent dental abscesses without obvious cause
references: Witkop CJ Jr. Dentin dysplasia. Oral Surg Oral Med Oral Pathol. 1972;33(5):661-670.
Wang S, et al. DSPP mutations in dentinogenesis imperfecta and dentin dysplasia. J Dent Res. 2011;90(11):1327-1332.
